thread.title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Bloodied By Warnings From Caterpillar and Nvidia

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Bloodied By Warnings From Caterpillar and Nvidia
text:
Shutterstock photo Weighed by event risk and disappointing quarterly results from chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Dow component Caterpillar ( CAT ), Wall Street limped into the start of the heaviest week o f earnings with significant losses. Led by losses in the technology and healthcare sectors, the S&P 500 is negative for the first time in four days.
De-risking was already in play before Monday's open as global investors were bracing for a week peppered with geopolitical and economic landmines that amplified uncertainty. US/China trade talks resume this week, while the UK parliament votes on the second Brexit bill, the first of which was resoundingly rejected by MPs. Additionally, a busy week for quarterly results ends with the closely-watched labor marke t report on Friday. This week, 3M ( MMM ), Apple ( AAPL ), Boeing ( BA ), McDonalds (MCD), Qualcomm (QCOM), Tesla (TSLA) and General Electric (GE) are just a fraction of headliners reporting this week.
Magnifying the defensive tone were revenue warnings from trade-sensitive Caterpillar and Nvidia, both of which lowered FY19 targets because of challenging economic conditions in China. The once high-flying Nvidia was down as much as 18% after the chipmaker warned that "deteriorating macro-economic conditions" -- specifically in China -- resulted in a "disappointing quarter."
Bullish economic data failed to dent the bearish price action on Wall Street even as the Chicago Fed national activity index rose to a 4-month high, and the Dallas Fed manufacturing index was jerked into positive territory.
European markets closed with outsized losses as China's slowing economy and fading optimism before the next Brexit vote set the major indices back as much as 1%. Job cuts at Tesco, the UK's largest grocery chain, resulted from the "challenging and uncertain economic climate."
Related markets reflect the flight to safety with gold holding above $1,300 per ounce and silver at its highest level in three weeks. Treasury yields are roughly 2 basis point lower despite a deluge of supply this week. Oil futures fell 3%-4% on global growth worries and supply pressures after the recent Baker Hughes rig count. Turmoil in Venezuela is also a factor as protests in the capital and high-ranking military defections pushes the country closer to anarchy.
Stocks in the news Monday include Brazilian iron-ore producer Vale (VALE), plummeting as much as 17% after the firm cut its dividend payment and stock buybacks. The government froze its assets after a deadly dam accident that killed at least 60 people. Tesla (TSLA) shares are losing ground on reports Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund hedged its 4.9% stake in the carmaker in the event the stock price falls.
Crude oil was down $2.10 to $51.59 per barrel. Natural gas was down $0.21 to $2.97 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $4.50 to $1,302.50 an ounce, while silver was up $0.07 to $15.75 an ounce. Copper was down $0.05 to $2.68 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was down 3.69% to $10.84 with the United States Natural Gas Fund down 5.07% to $26.01. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 0.65% to 21.28 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.21% to $123.12. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.24% to $14.78.
